clue.text: Facial adornment in charming location

definitions.meaning: a small dark mark or patch on the face, once worn deliberately as decoration
a scenic place that visitors flock to admire

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a mole or patch worn on the cheek and a picturesque place, two separate senses.

clue.text: Card game in place of tea party

definitions.meaning: a whist-like card game named after the American city
the city where colonists dumped British tea into the harbour in 1773

explanation.definitionFit: The Massachusetts city gave its name to an old trick-taking card game and hosted the famous 1773 tea protest.

clue.text: Damage, say, old tower

parts.note: to mar something is to damage it
to tell is to say

explanation.surface: Someone notes the damage done to an ancient tower.
explanation.walkthrough: MARTELLO towers are small round coastal forts built around Britain during the Napoleonic wars.
explanation.definitionFit: A Martello is a kind of round defensive coastal fort, so the word alone names that sort of building.

clue.text: Song for which the man moves last section to front

indicators.note: the closing letters of the phrase the man are shifted to its start

explanation.surface: A song in which a man shifts the final part to the opening.
explanation.walkthrough: Write THEMAN; taking its last section AN and putting it at the front gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthem is a solemn or rousing song, such as a national hymn.

clue.text: Man's man, maybe, I speak ill of

parts.note: to slander someone is to speak ill of them

explanation.surface: Someone admits to badmouthing another man's best friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, an island between Britain and Ireland, so a Manxman is one example of an island dweller; 'maybe' marks the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Isle of Man lives on an island, so he is one instance of an island dweller.

clue.text: A lot can be said for this kind of entertainment

indicators.note: spoken out, the word for one's lot matches the sound of the outdoor festivity

parts.note: one's lot in life is one's fate

explanation.surface: Much praise could be offered for this type of show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot' reads as 'plenty', but it is one's lot, one's destiny; spoken, that word matches the summer-fair word.
explanation.definitionFit: A fête is an outdoor fair with stalls and games, a form of public entertainment.

clue.text: The writer has distinctive way to work, note

parts.note: the writer of a clue refers to themself as me
MO is modus operandi, a characteristic method of working

explanation.surface: An author with a signature working method writes a reminder.
explanation.definitionFit: A memo is a short written message or reminder, a kind of note.

clue.text: Manage to include small cars in trade arrangement

indicators.note: the rearranged word is made to take in the cars, so they sit within it
an arrangement of trade means its letters are put in a new order

parts.note: Minis are small British cars

explanation.surface: A dealer contrives to fit some little cars into a trade deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trade arrangement' reads as a business deal, but 'arrangement' is the anagram signal and 'to include' the container; Minis are the classic small British cars.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer an organisation or affair is to run or manage it.

clue.text: A couple of non-alcoholic drinks one can buy in bars

parts.note: milk is a soft drink
hot chocolate is a soft drink, often just called chocolate

explanation.surface: Two soft drinks are on offer in pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' suggests pubs, where the drinks would be sold, but it means slabs of confectionery.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk chocolate is sold as confectionery shaped into slabs, so a shopper buys it in that form.

clue.text: A lot must change for the final reckoning

indicators.note: the words a lot must are to be changed, rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: Plenty has to alter before the last calculation is done.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum total is the overall amount reached when everything is added up, the final tally.

clue.text: Bliss English found in port

indicators.note: the abbreviation for English is located within the harbour word

parts.note: a haven is a harbour or port

explanation.surface: Joy for an Englishman discovered at the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaven is used for a state of supreme happiness, as in 'pure heaven'.

clue.text: Religious book converted many in hard left

indicators.note: the jumbled word sits between the two single letters

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: the word many is converted into a new arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A holy text won over many people on the hardline political left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted many' suggests missionaries winning souls, but 'converted' is the anagram signal, and 'hard left' is simply two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymnal is a book of hymns used in church worship.

clue.text: Stage performer in company, kind of average

parts.note: the median is one type of statistical average

explanation.surface: An actor in a troupe is merely middling.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedian is an entertainer who performs humorous acts on stage.

clue.text: Bring in charge after a game, acknowledging fault

indicators.note: the bringing and charge pieces follow the article and the sport

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
to get something is to fetch or bring it

explanation.surface: A player is brought up on a charge after a match and admits being wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Being apologetic means expressing regret, owning up to having done wrong.

clue.text: Concentration put into changing opera into different work

indicators.note: the abbreviated word is placed inside the rearranged letters
the words opera and into are changed into a new order

parts.note: conc is the abbreviation for concentration, as in chemistry

explanation.surface: Focus is needed to turn an opera into a different piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' is the anagram signal and 'put into' the insertion; 'different' only rounds off the surface, and the abbreviation is the one used for solution strength in chemistry.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano concerto is a musical composition for soloist and orchestra, one kind of musical work.

clue.text: Bill clergyman assembled right

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill
a curate is an assistant clergyman

explanation.surface: Bill and a vicar's assistant gathered correctly.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate means correct, exactly true, as in a right answer.

clue.text: Singer in bars links modern composer with old one, say

parts.note: John Cage was a twentieth-century American composer

indicators.note: the word say signals the old composer's name is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: William Byrd was a Tudor English composer

explanation.surface: A musician in a pub connects a modern composer with an older one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' hints at music or pubs, but the singer is a songbird behind cage bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A cagebird is a songbird such as a canary kept in a cage, so it sings behind its bars.

clue.text: Played separately, so acts oddly inside

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Played separately, so acts oddly inside' cannot give STACCATO: SO around the anagram of ACTS gives the wrong letters (two S, one C, one A); STACCATO needs TACCAT inside SO, so a word such as 'cat' seems missing and no source confirms the printed wording.
annotationWithheld.clue: Played separately, so acts oddly inside

clue.text: A right to cover all points in response

indicators.note: the article and the letter for right go round the compass letters, covering them

parts.note: N, S, W and E are all four compass points

explanation.surface: A right that covers every point raised in a reply.
explanation.definitionFit: An answer is a reply given in response to a question.

clue.text: Swine partly cured? Nonsense!

definitions.meaning: the cured hind leg of a pig, a bacon cut
an old informal word for humbug or rubbish talk

explanation.definitionFit: Gammon is a ham cut from a cured pig's leg, and also old slang for foolish talk.

clue.text: Something that distresses me in Indian city

parts.note: me turned possessive gives my
a sore is a painful or distressing spot

explanation.surface: Something in an Indian city is troubling the writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mysore, now officially Mysuru, is a city in the southern Indian state of Karnataka.

clue.text: Sun exposure led to his downfall

definitions.text: Sun exposure led to his downfall

parts.words: Sun exposure led to his downfall
parts.note: reads like a sunburn warning, but it is the Greek myth of the youth whose wax wings melted when he flew too near the sun

explanation.surface: A cautionary tale of someone ruined by too much sunbathing.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Daedalus's son flew too close to the sun, the wax in his wings melted and he fell into the sea.

clue.text: Stylishness of short young woman

indicators.note: short means the word is cut, losing its final letter

parts.note: chick is slang for a young woman

explanation.surface: Elegance belonging to a petite girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' looks like a description of the woman's height, but it trims CHICK to drop its K.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic as a noun means elegance and style.

clue.text: American done in, subject to sudden attack

parts.note: bushed is informal for exhausted, done in

explanation.surface: A worn-out American is set upon without warning.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambushed means attacked by surprise from a concealed position.

clue.text: Stars as cub

definitions.meaning: the constellation Ursa Minor, containing the Pole Star

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the constellation Ursa Minor and, read plainly, a bear's young.

clue.text: Cats and dogs artist has at home?

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
in means at home

explanation.surface: A painter keeps cats and dogs in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cats and dogs' looks like pets, but it is the idiom 'raining cats and dogs'.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy downpour is described as coming down cats and dogs, so the phrase stands for wet weather.
